⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **p2, a protocol narrowing handled directly in 18.x:** `LocaleSchema` still accepts a single-word language name (`Chinese`), which the #25822 changeset says is refused. Refuse it with the same refusal text, in `translation.zod.ts` and in the shared `SYS_USER_LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, with an ADR-0087 entry. `Skills-docs:` is owed (#26369 B). Found by the 18.2.0 wave-2 sweep (#25807).

Premise check and wait · `domain:spec` seat 3 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP` · 2026-10-27T05:19Z · ⛔ not a claim, no label change

**Premise: holds** (`origin/main` `c91544a4`). `LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE` at `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts:31` is still `/^[A-Za-z]{2,8}(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$/`, so a 2–8 letter word such as `Chinese` passes. The docblock above it (lines 16–30) and `LOCALE_TAG_REFUSAL` both say a language name is refused. `SYS_USER_LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts:33`) carries the same string. The refusal row in `translation.test.ts:56` pins only `'Chinese (Simplified)'`. The triage route (refuse it, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, an ADR-0087 entry, `Skills-docs:` owed) stands.

**Waiting on:** #25785 (PR #26159, in flight on `domain:spec` seat 2). Both cards are `area:i18n`, and their file surfaces intersect on `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`. So the one-in-flight-per-axis rule holds this card until PR #26159 lands, the same as #26128. Spec seat 1 left this card to spec seat 3's i18n lane, and seat 3 dispatches it when #26159 merges, after judging it by file surface against #26128 (whose edits sit in the `TranslationItemSchema` region of the same file).

Seat reading on the two pins the thread measured as asserting the opposite: `sys-user-locale-write-contract.test.ts:205-215` pins `Japanese` as accepted, and `recipient-locale-shape-parity.test.ts:72-82` pins `null` as shape-legal and asks readers not to tighten the shared regex. The governing text is the maintainer ruling of 2026-09-03 (option B) the plugin-auth file quotes: "a malformed value is refused loudly by the column's BCP-47 shape check". It names a SHAPE check and fixes no subtag length. A 2–3 letter primary language subtag is still shape, not membership (`xx` stays accepted, unknown tags still fall to the delivery ladder), so the ruling is unchanged and the two pins are a test author's reading of the old 2–8 shape. They move with this card: `Japanese` and `null` become shape-refused on both sides, the parity pin keeps the two spellings byte-identical, and `NOTHING_LITERALS` stays as a read-side floor. Clause-② is `no (narrowing)` per the seat rule for narrowing a published accept set (the dispatch order's `yes (narrowing)` is corrected here; precedent #25983).
